history_vintages.why: 'The Charles Schwab Corporation (CSC) ... engages, through its subsidiaries (collectively referred to as the Company, and primarily located in San Francisco except as indicated), in securities brokerage, banking, and related financial services.' 'Developments in the business, economic, and geopolitical environment could negatively impact the Company’s business.' 'There has been aggressive price competition in the Company’s industry, which may continue in the future.' (FY2006 10-K); DURABLE, risk 2: the 10-K ties results to markets, rates and investor engagement and names price competition, a cycle and a competitive field, and does not call its own business cyclical (the JPM, LOW and SHW reading); no theme in taxonomy_eras.json is live for a securities broker and bank on these dates (OFFSHORE is scoped to IT services), so the watch list is empty and these words stay here (the PEP obesity rule)

eps_first_excluded.2002: a distorted year (the AAPL FY2002 test): the items the FY2002 10-K excludes from adjusted operating income (restructuring charges of $373M, goodwill and other impairment charges of $61M and merger- and acquisition-related charges of $27M, less a $22M extraordinary gain: $287M after tax) exceed the year's $117M income from continuing operations as the FY2006 10-K restates it ($0.09 a share); the adjusted figure is in dollars on the earlier basis (U.S. Trust in, no per-share figure), so none excludes them on the continuing-operations basis; FY2001 ($0.05, with $208M of excluded items after tax) precedes it, and the history and the P/E window start with FY2003 (the JPM FY2002 rule)
